campbell.title: Campbell City Council — August 18, 2026
campbell.summary: The Campbell City Council considered several administrative items, including choosing voting delegates for the 2026 League of California Cities annual conference, a resolution amending the city's agreement for city clerk services, and a grant acceptance presented by the police captain on behalf of the police department. The council also took up a governance-related update concerning the BART Silicon Valley project.
keyTopics: Designation of voting delegates for the 2026 League of California Cities annual conference
Resolution amending the first amended agreement for city clerk services
Grant acceptance on behalf of the police department, presented by the police captain
Governance update regarding the BART Silicon Valley project

saratoga.title: Saratoga City Council — September 2, 2026
saratoga.summary: The Saratoga City Council reviewed routine items like meeting minutes, vendor payments, and the Treasurer's Report, and considered draft responses to two Santa Clara County Civil Grand Jury reports on pothole damage claims and VTA's oversight of the BART Silicon Valley Phase II project. The council also took up several policy items, including support for a state data transparency bill, a contract for a transportation impact fee study, forming a committee to look at alternative policing services, and the future of the Saratoga Blossom Festival.
keyTopics: Draft responses to Civil Grand Jury reports on pothole damage claims and VTA's management of BART Silicon Valley Phase II
Support for AB 1761, which addresses data transparency for utility rate charges
An $85,000 contract with Fehr and Peers for a Transportation Impact Fee study
Forming an Ad-Hoc Committee to review alternative policing services in Saratoga
The future of the Saratoga Blossom Festival and continued involvement in the Cities Association of Santa Clara County

los-altos.title: Los Altos City Council — August 25, 2026
los-altos.summary: The Los Altos City Council considered several infrastructure and housing items, including a roof replacement contract for the History Museum, an EV charger installation project at the Maintenance Yard, and completion of the Woodland Library patio expansion. The council also held a public hearing on renaming Lee Street to Tubman Street and reviewed two large condominium development proposals on First Street and Sherwood/Acacia Avenue.
keyTopics: Public hearing on renaming Lee Street to Tubman Street, with options to act now or refer to the Historical Commission for further study
Vesting Tentative Map approvals for 19 condominium units at 349 First Street and 33 units at Sherwood/Acacia Avenues
History Museum roof replacement contract with Diablo Roofing (not-to-exceed $147,500 plus 15% contingency)
Maintenance Yard EV Chargers construction contract with Bockmon & Woody Electric Co. (not-to-exceed $363,220)
Draft responses to Santa Clara County Civil Grand Jury reports on pothole damage claims and VTA's BART Silicon Valley Phase II oversight

los-gatos.title: Los Gatos Town Council — September 1, 2026
los-gatos.summary: The Los Gatos Town Council met to approve routine meeting minutes and consider a handful of administrative items, including vacating a public service easement on Cerro Vista, setting up preferential and time-limited parking in a neighborhood, and hiring a consultant for executive-related work.
keyTopics: Vacating a public service easement at 15995 Cerro Vista
Establishing preferential permit parking and time-limited parking
Authorizing a consultant agreement for executive services
Approval of minutes from several August 2026 Council meetings

san-jose.body: Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole
san-jose.title: San José Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole — September 2, 2026
san-jose.summary: The Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole considered the draft agenda for the September 15, 2026 meeting, including whether to add items or set specific times for discussion. The committee also reviewed the City Clerk's public record from August 20-27, 2026, and a study session on financing tools for economic development infrastructure. The September 8, 2026 meeting was canceled.
keyTopics: Cancellation of the September 8, 2026 meeting
Planning of the September 15, 2026 draft agenda, including possible new items and scheduling
Public record review for August 20-27, 2026
Study session on infrastructure financing tools for economic development

mountain-view.title: Mountain View Youth Advisory Committee — August 31, 2026
mountain-view.summary: Mountain View's Youth Advisory Committee opened its term with a team-building activity and a training session on public meeting rules, including the Brown Act and Robert's Rules of Order. Members also discussed the committee's overall purpose and began brainstorming ideas for its work plan for the upcoming fiscal year.
keyTopics: Team-building activity for committee members
Training on the Brown Act and Robert's Rules of Order
Discussion of the Youth Advisory Committee's role
Brainstorming for the FY 2026-27 work plan
Public comment period (oral communications)

sunnyvale.title: Sunnyvale City Council — August 25, 2026
sunnyvale.summary: The Sunnyvale City Council held a special meeting on August 25, 2026, that began with a closed session, followed by a separate public meeting focused on a presentation about updates to the CleanWater Program.
keyTopics: Closed session held ahead of the public meeting
Presentation and update on the CleanWater Program

cupertino.title: Cupertino City Council — September 1, 2026
cupertino.summary: This Cupertino City Council meeting opened with a report on matters discussed in closed session, followed by a reminder to the public and any advocates about the city's lobbyist registration and reporting requirements. The posted agenda highlights did not include additional substantive policy items beyond these two matters.
keyTopics: Report from closed session
Lobbyist registration and reporting requirements under Cupertino Municipal Code Chapter 2.100

santa-clara.title: Santa Clara City Council — August 25, 2026
santa-clara.summary: This Santa Clara City Council meeting was held in a hybrid format, allowing both in-person attendance and remote participation via Zoom or phone. One councilmember participated remotely from India.
keyTopics: Councilmember Chahal participated remotely from Panchkula, India
Meeting held in hybrid format with in-person and Zoom/phone participation options for the public

milpitas.title: Milpitas City Council — September 1, 2026
milpitas.summary: The Milpitas City Council, sitting as the board of the city's Successor Agency to the former Redevelopment Agency, considered routine housekeeping and financial items tied to winding down old redevelopment debt. This included confirming which city officials hold official Successor Agency roles and authorizing the sale of refunding bonds to refinance existing redevelopment-era debt.
keyTopics: Confirming and designating city officials as officers of the Successor Agency to the Redevelopment Agency
Authorizing issuance and sale of 2026 Tax Allocation Refunding Bonds to refinance Successor Agency debt

palo-alto.title: Palo Alto Economic Development Committee — August 26, 2026
palo-alto.summary: The Economic Development Committee reviewed a staff presentation on the city's Business Retention, Expansion, and Attraction (BRE/A) Strategy, which focuses on helping existing businesses stay and grow while attracting new ones to Palo Alto. The Committee also considered a monthly Economic Development Activity Report covering August 2026.
keyTopics: Presentation on the Business Retention, Expansion, and Attraction (BRE/A) Strategy
Monthly Economic Development Activity Report for August 2026
